summary.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue about INR4,108 crore, lead-acid up ~18%, but consolidated margin fell ~1.3pp to 8.8% on new-energy and input-cost pressure.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was about INR4,108 crore with lead-acid (about 94% of revenue) growing about 18% and new energy growing over 30% to about INR232 crore. Standalone EBITDA margin was about 10.1%, stable quarter-on-quarter but lower year-on-year due to elevated material costs (alloys, sulfuric acid, poly), Amaron Assist and factory-of-the-future spending, and a higher OEM mix. International revenue fell about 20% year-on-year on Middle East volume weakness. Board approved a ~INR2,320 crore LFP prismatic cell gigafactory (~5 GWh) and pack capacity to be completed in about 30 months, and the ePositive Lab started on October 26.

financial_highlights.value: about INR800 crore, of which INR500 crore in new energy
financial_highlights.change: against FY27 plan of about INR2,200 crore

segments.name: Automotive OEM
segments.commentary: OEM volumes grew about 17% in four-wheeler and over 30% in two-wheeler YoY. Price increases were passed through to two-wheeler OEM customers.

segments.name: Automotive aftermarket
segments.commentary: Domestic aftermarket volumes grew about 6-7% in both four-wheeler and two-wheeler YoY. Management says four-wheeler share is about 35% and two-wheeler share gained.

segments.name: Home energy (tubular and home UPS)
segments.commentary: Grew more than 50% YoY. Management estimates share gained 3-4 percentage points from an earlier 10-15%.

segments.name: Telecom and UPS
segments.commentary: Lead-acid telecom volumes spiked over 30% due to delays in annual lithium telecom pack negotiations with OEMs. Lithium telecom packs grew about 15% YoY. Combined telecom market share is above 60%. UPS volumes grew about 8%.

segments.name: New energy (BESS, packs, cells)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR232 crore, up over 30%. Telecom packs grew about 15% YoY, while EV volumes faced demand headwinds. Losses come from product development costs and depreciation on labs.

guidance_outlook: Management expects lead-acid volume or revenue growth of 8-10% in the medium term, with aftermarket at 6-8% and home tubular at up to 10%.

Margin improvement of about 1.5% is possible from cost normalisation, recycling and international recovery. A further about 2% (optimistic 2.5%) is possible after throughput initiatives and input costs ease.
Standalone margin will improve after Amaron Assist moves to a subsidiary, but by less than the 1% impact cited.
BESS: trial runs in December, operations from January or February. FY28 utilisation estimated at 50-60% of 5 GWh, full utilisation by FY29. About 30% of phase-1 capacity could go to exports.
Capex of about INR2,200 crore planned for FY27, with about INR1,600 crore in new energy.
ROCE recovery expected in about 2-3 years, as new energy needs 8-10 GWh scale for optimum returns.

qa_highlights.question: Is 6% aftermarket growth soft, and has share been maintained? Any Q3 price action?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says growth of 6-7% is in line with industry. Four-wheeler aftermarket share is about 35%, and two-wheeler share has gained. Further price hikes in Q3 depend on acid and poly costs and competition.

qa_highlights.question: BESS utilisation path and competitive intensity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 50-60% utilisation in FY28 and full 5 GWh by FY29. It does not see margin pressure from new capacity, since demand is expected to outstrip supply and about 70% of cells are still imported.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable EBITDA margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says underlying margin is about 11% before the 1% strategic spend. Another 1.5% is possible from input costs, recycling and international recovery, and a further 2-2.5% after throughput initiatives and acid, poly and sulphur normalise.

qa_highlights.question: ROE and ROCE trajectory after heavy capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says lead-acid ROCE can return to 20-23%. Consolidated ROCE, adjusted for new energy, was about 18% in FY26. Recovery is expected in about 2-3 years, as new energy reaches 8-10 GWh scale.

qa_highlights.question: Will standalone margins improve after Amaron Assist is moved to a subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, but management says the gain will be less than 1%, because the 1% includes manufacturing-capability spend as well as Amaron Assist.

qa_highlights.question: Lithium and NMC progress and customer feedback?
qa_highlights.answer: About 2,000 NMC B-samples are under internal testing, with OEM handover in about a couple of months. LFP timelines are not yet firm.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (acid, poly, alloys, sulphur, separators, rupee depreciation) with 2-3 month lag in aftermarket pass-through.
International business recovery from the Middle East decline (about -20% YoY), tied to geopolitics and freight costs.
BESS ramp-up, which depends on commissioning in Dec-Feb and on utilisation of 50-60% in FY28. Import-cell dependence creates a 10-15% cost gap.
Return ratios (ROCE/ROE) will stay under pressure until new energy scales. Management guides 2-3 years.
Lithium cell timelines: NMC handover to OEMs in about a couple of months, LFP timeline not committed.
Recycling margin benefit delayed by lead scrap availability and local lead price rises after import disruptions.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand and the lead-acid franchise, but cautious near term on margins, international volumes, and lithium timelines. Management repeatedly refused to give firm dates for LFP and ROCE recovery. Several answers were framed as "optimistic" scenarios.
key_quotes: So, the demand per se is not a constraint because as you know, the banking facilities that are currently operational in some of the states will slowly move into a compulsory storage that needs to be created at the grid level.
Because a 20% de-growth on international business which is a very good margin business for me, is really hurting the overall bottom line.
So, the lithium business cannot be built overnight, and it requires some level of capability building to be done before we actually achieve independence and then improve that business from there.
capex_capacity: Board approved next-phase capex of about INR2,320 crore for a prismatic cell gigafactory (LFP-based, about 5 GWh) and pack assembly capacity, to be completed within about 30 months; cell plant initially for stationary, later mobility applications.

FY27 capex plan about INR2,200 crore, of which about INR1,600 crore is new energy and includes payments for the new cell and pack plans; about INR800 crore spent in H1 FY27, of which INR500 crore in new energy.

BESS: acceptance steps on machinery completed; trial runs in December, operations likely January or February. Ramp-up over next two to three months; about 30% of phase-1 5 GWh capacity could go to exports if conditions are met.
Utilisation expected at 50-60% of 5 GWh in FY28 and full utilisation by FY29.
ePositive Lab commenced operations on October 26.

Lead-acid capacity: two-wheeler plants running about 95-100%; four-wheeler about 80-85%; no underutilisation expected for five to six years; possible debottlenecking or one to two additional four-wheeler lines. Telecom lead-acid line (about 30 million Ah per month) being repurposed for smaller batteries.
Cumulative invested to date: about INR2,100 crore in the subsidiary (new energy) and about INR700 crore in recycling facilities. Amaron Assist to be moved into a wholly owned subsidiary.
demand_pricing: Aftermarket volumes grew about 6-7% YoY in both four-wheeler and two-wheeler, in line with industry per management; four-wheeler aftermarket share about 35% maintained, two-wheeler share gained.
OEM volumes: four-wheeler about +17% YoY, two-wheeler over +30% YoY; price hike passed through to two-wheeler OEM customers.

Price actions: about 2% hike in Q2 FY27 and cumulative about 5% in H1 FY27; further Q3 hike depends on acid and poly costs and competition. Aftermarket pass-through lags input costs by about 2-3 months.

Input costs: raw acid prices rose from about INR10/kg to about INR43-44/kg; separator and alloy costs up; rupee depreciation; domestic lead prices higher after import disruption; battery export freight about 7-8 times higher.
Home energy (tubular and home UPS) grew more than 50% YoY; share gained about 3-4 percentage points from earlier 10-15%.
Telecom: lead-acid volumes spiked over 30% on delayed annual lithium telecom pack negotiations; lithium telecom packs grew about 15% YoY; combined market share above 60%; UPS volumes about +8%.
International revenue down about 20% YoY on Middle East volume drop; improved QoQ; management expects recovery and sees potential above 15% growth once geopolitics and supply chain stabilise.
Medium-term outlook: aftermarket 6-8%, home tubular up to 10%, lead-acid volume or revenue growth 8-10%; lead-acid UPS 6-7%.
New energy revenue about INR232 crore, up over 30%; EV volumes faced demand headwinds; telecom packs up about 15%.

BESS pricing about USD90-100 per kWh; assembly margin expected about 6-7% at operating level, ROCE accretive; import-cell cost disadvantage about 10-15% versus China, partly mitigated by government support such as ALMM-type protection.
Management sees no margin pressure from BESS competition as demand expected to outstrip supply; about 70% of cells still imported.
Lithium: about 2,000 NMC B-samples under internal testing, OEM handover in about a couple of months; LFP timeline not firm; dedicated team of 200-250 people on cell development.
